title: Getting a second person in: four planning tools, sign-up to the invite
question: How do these four planning tools get a second person into a new workspace, from sign-up to the invite, and what do the others do that Larkspur does not?
note: Larkspur, Thistle, Corbel and Halyard are fictional. Every screen is a schematic drawing made for this example, not a screenshot. Notes and scores are one reader's, from one sitting. Nothing was timed: Speed counts steps and typing.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.means: You can tell what to do next without reading twice.

dimensions.name: Speed
dimensions.means: Few steps and little typing to finish the stage.

dimensions.name: Transparency
dimensions.means: Costs, limits and consequences are shown before they bite.

dimensions.name: Engagement
dimensions.means: It gives a reason to come back or go further.

stages.name: Create the workspace

lanes.flow: Signup step 3 asks for teammates, then an empty Home

notes.t: Step 3 of 5 is "Invite your team", before the user has built anything, with three email fields and "Send invites".
"Skip for now" is plain text on the right, while "Send invites" is a button, so skipping is easy and the ask is easy to miss.
"Invite your whole team, free" gives no limit. The three fields match the "3 seats included" line the S3 invite dialog shows later.
Home says "Your workspace is ready" but shows only a 1 of 4 checklist. "Invite your team" is third and has no button.
The checklist keeps "Invite your team" in view, so a skipped invite is not lost.

clarity.why: One title, three fields and two clear exits on step 3; the skip link is plain text.

speed.why: Three emails to type, and the invite step adds a page to signup.

transparency.why: "Free" is claimed with no limit, and no price is on the page.

trust.why: Skipping is quiet, but the invite stays on the Home checklist.

engagement.why: Asks for teammates before the first project and keeps the ask visible after.

lanes.verdict: Asks for teammates during signup, but leaves the limit on 'free' unsaid.
well: Puts the teammate ask in signup, before the first project.
Keeps 'Invite your team' on the Home checklist after a skip.
wrong: 'Invite your whole team, free' hides the three seat limit.
Skip is plain text and the checklist row has no button.
steal: A teammate step inside signup with three fields and a clear skip.

lanes.flow: Signup ends on a filled sample project with Share

notes.t: Two fields and one button, "Start with a sample". Nothing else stands between signup and the product.
There is no teammate ask and no cost line, so a second person is not mentioned until the user finds Share.

blocks: Replace the sample with your own

notes.t: "Replace the sample with your own" is the next job, with "Takes about two minutes" beside it.
Share sits top right on a sample page, before there is any real work to share.

clarity.why: Two fields and one button; the user always knows the next click.

speed.why: Signup ends in the product after two fields.

transparency.why: No cost or visibility line appears, but nothing is promised either.

trust.why: The sample is named as a sample and offers its own replacement.

engagement.why: A ready project gives something to do, but no second person is mentioned.

lanes.verdict: The shortest route into a working page, but it never asks about a second person.
well: A filled sample with a timed next step.
wrong: No teammate ask in signup.
Share appears on a sample page with nothing to share.
steal: Land on a filled sample so the first page is never empty.

lanes.flow: Signup connects the chat tool and lists who is there

screens.step: Is asked to connect the chat tool
blocks: Connect Parley to see who is already there.

blocks.sub: We read names and photos only

notes.t: "We read names and photos only" says what connecting Parley takes, right beside the Connect button.
Nothing says whether the people found here will cost anything once added. The S3 invite dialog shows $10 per month.

blocks: 12 people found. Choose who to add

notes.t: "12 people found" lists real colleagues with team names, so the user picks names instead of typing emails.
Nobody is ticked and the button reads "Add 0 people", so the default is to add nobody.
Offer one tick for "Add my team", and show the price on this screen.

clarity.why: "12 people found. Choose who to add" says the job; the button count is honest.

speed.why: Connect, tick names, add. No typing, but three taps and a connection.

transparency.why: Says what the connection reads, but not what adding people costs.

trust.why: Nobody is ticked and the button reads 'Add 0 people', so nothing happens by default.

engagement.why: Shows real colleagues by name, which gives a reason to go on.

lanes.verdict: Turns the invite into picking from real colleagues, but shows no price at that point.
well: States what connecting reads: names and photos only.
wrong: No price shown when people are added.
'You can add people later' is small text.
steal: A picker of real colleagues from the chat tool, with the count on the button.

lanes.flow: Signup promises a free trial, then an empty Home

blocks: Free for 14 days. No card needed.

notes.t: "Free for 14 days. No card needed." is the first thing on the page, in an accent banner.
Signup asks for no teammate. It is two fields and "Create workspace", then Home.
Home shows "Nothing here yet" and a five item checklist. "Invite your team" is last and has no button.
Two starts compete: the "New project" card and a checklist whose first open step is also a project.

clarity.why: Home has a project card and a five task checklist that both start with a project.

speed.why: Two fields in signup, but the invite is the last of five tasks.

transparency.why: "Free for 14 days. No card needed." is plain and first. Billing on S3 undercuts it.

trust.why: The free promise is clear here and is broken on the S3 Add member dialog.

engagement.why: Empty Home and no teammate ask; nothing pulls a second person in.

lanes.verdict: A plain, clear trial promise, but an empty Home that puts the invite last.
wrong: No teammate ask in signup.
'Invite your team' is the last task and has no button.

stages.finding: Thistle and Halyard ask for teammates in signup; Corbel and Larkspur do not, and Larkspur then puts the invite last on an empty Home.

best.why: The user picks named colleagues and the button says 'Add 0 people', so nothing is added by accident.
The invite is step 3 of 5 and stays on the Home checklist after a skip.

patterns.name: Ask for teammates before the first project
patterns.text: A signup step names or collects teammates while the user is still setting up, with a clear way to skip.

anti.name: The invite is a checklist row, not a button
anti.text: 'Invite your team' is listed with no action beside it, and sits last or third.

anti.name: A sample page with Share before any real work
anti.text: Share is offered on a page with nothing of the user's own to share.

ideal.name: Ask in signup
ideal.text: After the workspace name, show one step to add teammates, with a skip.

ideal.name: Name real people
ideal.text: Offer colleagues from a connected tool, or three email fields. Show the count on the button.

ideal.name: Say the cost here
ideal.text: State the price and when billing starts, on the same screen.

ideal.name: Keep the ask on Home
ideal.text: If skipped, leave 'Invite your team' with a button on the checklist.

gaps.title: Signup never asks for a teammate
gaps.today: Two fields and 'Create workspace', then an empty Home.
gaps.fix: Add a teammate step to signup with a skip, like Thistle's step 3.

gaps.title: The invite is the last task and has no button
gaps.today: 'Invite your team' is the fifth checklist row on an empty Home.
gaps.fix: Move it up and give it a button.

gaps.title: No real colleagues to pick from
gaps.fix: Offer a connected chat tool and list people by name, as Halyard does.

stages.name: Make the first project

lanes.flow: A project table that only lists You, plus a nudge

blocks: Projects are better with a team.

notes.t: The banner "Projects are better with a team." appears on the project page itself.
"Invite" is a second line of text, not a button, and the banner copy is generic.
Every row in the Assign column says "You", so the table shows a one person plan.

screens.step: Opens the Assign menu on a task

blocks.sub: Only you are in this workspace

notes.t: The Assign menu offers only "You", says "Only you are in this workspace" and ends with "Invite teammates".
The same ask as the banner on the previous screen, so the user meets it twice in one project.

clarity.why: The banner and the Assign menu say what to do and where.

speed.why: One click from the banner or the menu to the invite.

transparency.why: Says 'Only you are in this workspace', but gives no cost at the nudge.

trust.why: The menu offers only 'You' and says why, so nothing is hidden.

engagement.why: Two nudges inside the work, one at the point of assigning.

lanes.verdict: Raises the invite where work is assigned, but the banner copy is generic.
well: The Assign menu says 'Only you are in this workspace' and offers 'Invite teammates'.
wrong: 'Invite' is text on the banner, not a button.
The table still shows only 'You'.
steal: An Assign menu that ends in an Invite button.

lanes.flow: Every page says Only you, Share stays top right

notes.t: "Only you" with Dana's avatar sits under the page title and tells the user who can see this page.
It is a status line only. Nothing invites anyone, and "Share" is the only way out.
The second page repeats "Only you" and "Share" unchanged. The cue is steady but does not escalate.
Change the line once there are two pages, for example "Only you. Share this page."

clarity.why: 'Only you' under the title is easy to read.

speed.why: Share is always top right, one click away.

transparency.why: Shows who can see the page, but not what sharing costs.

trust.why: The visibility line is steady on both pages.

engagement.why: The cue is a status, not a prompt, and does not change on page two.

lanes.verdict: Always shows who can see a page, but only as a status that never asks.
wrong: No text invites anyone.
The cue does not escalate.
steal: A visibility line under every page title.

lanes.flow: A prompt appears after the third item

screens.step: Adds the third item to a plan

notes.t: "Ready to show someone?" appears right after the third row, when the plan has something to show.
The card offers "Preview", not "Invite", so the first ask is one step short of an invite.

blocks: Choose a person to preview as

notes.t: The user picks from three named colleagues with team names. Jordan, Priya and Mei came from the 12 listed in S1.
No invite button on this screen. The user previews and must find the invite elsewhere.

clarity.why: 'Ready to show someone?' says why the card is there; Preview is one step off Invite.

speed.why: The prompt arrives on its own after item three and picks from named people.

transparency.why: Says what the preview shows, not what an invite costs; price appears on S3.

trust.why: Preview sends nothing, so the user can look without committing.

engagement.why: Times the ask to when there is something to show, and uses people from S1.

lanes.verdict: Asks at the moment there is something to show, but offers Preview, not Invite.
well: Names three colleagues from the S1 list.
wrong: No invite button on the preview screen.
steal: A prompt that appears once the plan has three items.

lanes.flow: A project table, Owner is You, no mention of others

notes.t: The table has an Owner column and its only value is "You". Nothing on the screen mentions another person.
Put "Only you" and an "Invite" button next to the project name.
The checklist reads 2 of 5, but the table holds three items with due dates. Compare the S1 Home tasks "Add three items" and "Set a due date".
Nothing here leads to "Invite your team", the fifth task counted in the 2 of 5.

clarity.why: The table is readable, but the checklist count does not match the work.

speed.why: Items go in easily, but nothing points to the next step.

transparency.why: The checklist reads 2 of 5 with the first four tasks done by the screen.

trust.why: A progress count that does not move teaches the user to ignore it.

engagement.why: No mention of other people on either screen.

lanes.verdict: A tidy project table, but it never mentions anyone else.
well: Items and due dates are quick to add.
The checklist is shown on the project page.
wrong: The count says 2 of 5 with three items and dates entered.
No cue that others can join.

stages.finding: Thistle and Halyard raise the invite while the user works; Corbel only says 'Only you'; Larkspur does not mention other people on either screen.

best.why: The prompt arrives after the third item, when there is something to show, and lists named people.
The Assign menu says 'Only you are in this workspace' and offers 'Invite teammates'.

patterns.name: Ask at the point of need
patterns.text: The invite is raised inside the work, on a prompt or a menu, not only in settings.

patterns.name: Say who is in the workspace
patterns.text: The page says 'Only you' or 'Only you are in this workspace' next to the work.

anti.name: A table of one person
anti.text: Owner or Assign columns that only ever say 'You', with no cue that others can join.

anti.name: A progress count that does not move
anti.text: The checklist reads 2 of 5 with the first four tasks done by the screen.

ideal.name: Say who is here
ideal.text: Put 'Only you' next to the project name.

ideal.name: Prompt when there is something to show
ideal.text: After the third item, ask 'Ready to show someone?'.

ideal.name: Offer invite, not only preview
ideal.text: Put an Invite button beside the people listed.

gaps.title: No prompt to invite while the user works
gaps.today: The project page never mentions another person.
gaps.fix: Show a prompt after the third item, as Halyard does.

gaps.title: The Assign step has no invite
gaps.today: Owner is 'You' on every row and nothing offers anyone else.
gaps.fix: Make the owner cell open a menu that ends in 'Invite teammates', as Thistle does.

gaps.title: The checklist count is wrong
gaps.today: It reads 2 of 5 with items and due dates already in.
gaps.fix: Count each task as the work is done.
gaps.benchmarkNote: No app on the board shows a checklist count moving, so there is no benchmark.

stages.name: Bring someone in

lanes.flow: An invite dialog with a seat line in small text

notes.t: The invite dialog sits on People, a top level nav item, with one field and "Send invite".
"3 seats included, then $9 per member" does not say how many seats are used.
S1 said "Invite your whole team, free". Here the fourth person costs $9, and signup never said so.

screens.step: Sends the invite and sees it pending

notes.t: The table shows jordan@ as "Pending" with a "Member" role, and a toast says "Invite sent".
Nothing shows what Jordan will see or which project they land in.

clarity.why: The invite is one dialog with one field, on a nav item named People.

speed.why: Open People, type one email, send. Two steps.

transparency.why: The seat line shows the price before sending, but not how many seats are used.

trust.why: Pending is shown, but S1 said 'free' with no limit.

engagement.why: Confirms the invite, but not what Jordan will see.

lanes.verdict: A quick, honest invite dialog, but the pending row says nothing of what happens next.
well: People is a top level item.
A toast and a pending row confirm the send.
wrong: No view of what the invitee will see.
'Free' on S1 and $9 here are not tied together.
steal: A People item in the main nav with the invite dialog on it.

lanes.flow: A share dialog with a link, then a guest viewing

blocks.sub: Anyone with the link can view. Guests are free, forever

notes.t: "Anyone with the link can view. Guests are free, forever" states the cost and the reach in one line.
"Can comment" is off, so a guest can read but not take part.

screens.step: Copies the link, a guest opens it

notes.t: "1 guest viewing" with "Dana" and "+1": a second person is on the page in two actions, with no typing.
A viewing guest is not an active member. No Corbel screen gives a member price or a way to upgrade a guest.

clarity.why: Share dialog, link and one button; the guest view is shown next.

speed.why: Copy a link and a guest is in. No typing.

transparency.why: Says who can view and that guests are free, but no member price on any screen.

trust.why: The link scope is disclosed, with comments off by default.

engagement.why: A guest arrives fast, but can only look and nothing offers an upgrade.

lanes.verdict: The fastest way to get a second person on the page, but a guest only looks.
wrong: Comments are off by default.
No path from guest to member.
steal: A view link that makes a second person appear with no typing.

lanes.flow: Preview as the guest, then an invite that names the price

blocks.sub: This is what Jordan will see

notes.t: "Previewing as Jordan" and two rows tagged "Hidden from guests" show the invitee's view before anything is sent.
This is a guest view. The next screen invites Jordan as a member, so the preview may not match what they get.
"Salary band notes" is not among the three items on the S2 plan, so the preview shows a row the plan did not.

blocks.sub: Jordan joins as a member: $10 per month, billed from the end of your trial

notes.t: "Jordan joins as a member: $10 per month, billed from the end of your trial" gives price and date before "Send invite".
The S1 list let the user add people with no price shown. The price appears only here.

clarity.why: Preview, then a named invite. Each screen has one job.

speed.why: Two taps and no typing, because the name is already known.

transparency.why: The dialog gives the price and the billing start before 'Send invite'.

trust.why: The preview is a guest view, but the invite makes a member, so the match is unclear.

engagement.why: The user sees the invitee's view first, which gives a reason to go ahead.

lanes.verdict: Shows both the invitee's view and the price, but the preview is a guest view for a member invite.
well: Price and billing date in the dialog.
wrong: Preview and invite roles differ.
A 'Salary band notes' row is not on the S2 plan.
steal: Show the invite's price and billing start in the dialog.
Preview as the invitee before sending.

lanes.flow: Settings, Members, then an Add member dialog

notes.t: The invite lives under Settings, then Members. The nav has no People or Share item.
The Members table shows Dana as "Paid" during a trial that signup called free for 14 days.

blocks.sub: Adding a member starts billing today: $12 per month

notes.t: "Adding a member starts billing today: $12 per month" contradicts "Free for 14 days. No card needed." on S1 signup.
The price is on the dialog before the click, as Thistle and Halyard also do.
Use Halyard's wording: billed from the end of the trial.

clarity.why: Add member is clear once found, but the path is Settings then Members.

speed.why: Home, Settings, Members, Add member, type an email: four steps.

transparency.why: The $12 and 'billing today' are on the dialog before the click.

trust.why: 'Billing today' contradicts the S1 'No card needed', and Dana is 'Paid' in a trial.

engagement.why: No preview, no project link, nothing for the invitee.

lanes.verdict: States the price before the click, but hides the invite and contradicts the trial promise.
well: The price is in the dialog.
wrong: The invite is under Settings.
'Starts billing today' contradicts the signup.
Nothing shows what the invitee sees.

stages.finding: Halyard shows the invitee's view and the price before sending; Larkspur hides the invite in Settings and says billing starts today after promising no card.

best.why: The dialog gives price and billing start, and the invitee's view is previewed first.
A shared link gets a second person on the page with no typing.

patterns.name: Price in the invite dialog
patterns.text: The invite dialog states what the new person costs before the button.

patterns.name: The invite is one click from the work
patterns.text: A People item or a Share button sits in the main view.

anti.name: Billing that starts at the invite
anti.text: 'Starts billing today' after a trial that promised no card.

anti.name: A guest who can only look
anti.text: Comments are off and no upgrade path appears.

ideal.name: Find it in one click
ideal.text: A People item or a Share button, never Settings.

ideal.name: Show what they see
ideal.text: Preview the invitee's view, in the role they will get.

ideal.name: Say the price and the date
ideal.text: '$X per month, billed from the end of your trial'.

ideal.name: Confirm and attach
ideal.text: Show the pending row, and say which project they land in.

gaps.title: 'Billing starts today' contradicts the trial promise
gaps.today: S1 says 'No card needed'; the Add member dialog says billing starts today at $12.
gaps.fix: Word it as billed from the end of the trial.

gaps.title: The invite is under Settings, then Members
gaps.today: Four steps from Home and no People item.
gaps.fix: Add People to the main nav, as Thistle does.

gaps.title: No view of what the invitee will see
gaps.today: The dialog has an email field and a role.
gaps.fix: Add a preview as the invitee, in the role they get.

gaps.title: No zero cost way to bring someone in
gaps.today: Every second person is a paid seat.
gaps.fix: Offer a view link for guests.

principles.name: Ask before the page is empty
principles.text: Thistle and Halyard raise teammates in signup. Larkspur lists the invite last on an empty Home.

principles.name: Raise the invite where the work is
principles.text: The strongest cues are the Assign menu and the prompt after item three, not a setting.

principles.name: Say who is here, on every page
principles.text: 'Only you' tells the user the workspace is solo. Larkspur never says it.

principles.name: Say the price when you ask
principles.text: Halyard and Thistle price the seat in the dialog. Larkspur does, but contradicts its own trial.

principles.name: Let the invitee be seen before it is sent
principles.text: Halyard previews the invitee's view. Nobody else does, and Larkspur has nothing.
